dervis-irab:1-4.t:
* Vocabulary:
(عَمَدٍ): with two fatḥas. The views of the lexicographers are confused about it. Some said it is a plural of ʿimād not according to rule, the regular plural being ʿumud, with ḍamma on the ʿayn and the mīm. It was also said that ʿamad is a plural of ʿimād in meaning, that is, it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ), not a formal plural. What is in al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj is: "al-ʿamūd is that on which a house or other thing stands, and a rod of iron; its plural is aʿmida, ʿumud and ʿamad." Someone said:
ʿAmad is the plural of ʿamūd, and in the speech of the Arabs only four words came on this pattern: adīm and adam, ʿamūd and ʿamad, afīq and afaq, ihāb and ahab. Al-Farrāʾ added a fifth: qaḍīm and qaḍam, meaning deeds of parchment and skins.
(صِنْوانٌ): al-ṣinw, with kasra, fatḥa or ḍamma on the ṣād, is a palm tree with two heads whose root is one; two are ṣinwān and the plural is ṣinwān, with kasra on the ṣād in both. In al-Mukhtār: "When two or three palms come out of a single root, each one of them is a ṣinw, two are ṣinwān, and the plural is ṣinwān" — that is, it is declinable (muʿrab). In al-Asās: "Trees that are ṣinwān: from a single root, each one being a ṣinw. And figuratively: he is his full brother and his ṣinw. [The poet] said:
أتتركني وأنت أخي وصنوي ... فيا للناس للأمر العجيب
(Will you abandon me, when you are my brother and my twin? O people, what a strange thing!)
And two wells that are ṣinwān are close to one another. Its diminutive is ṣunayy. Laylā al-Akhyaliyya said:
أنابغ لم تنبغ ولم تك أولا ... وكنت صنيّا بين صدّين مجهلا
(O Nābigha, you never rose to eminence and were never first; you were a little well between two mountainsides, unknown.)
that is, an unknown well between two mountains." Some lexicographers said: "Al-ṣinw is a branch that shares one root with another branch, and [it means] the like." In the hadith: «A man's paternal uncle is the ṣinw of his father», that is, his like, or because a single root joins them. Nakhīl and nakhl have one meaning, and the singular is nakhla. [The poet] said:
ألا يا نخلة من ذات عرق ... عليك ورحمة الله السلام
(O palm tree of Dhāt ʿIrq, upon you — and the mercy of Allah — be peace.)
The wording of Abū Ḥayyān:
"Al-ṣinw is a branch that shares one root with another; its basic meaning is 'the like', and from it the paternal uncle is called ṣinw. Its plural in the dialect of the Ḥijāz is ṣinwān, with kasra on the ṣād, like qinw and qinwān, and with ḍamma in the dialect of Tamīm and Qays, like dhiʾb and dhuʾbān. One also says ṣanwān, with fatḥa on the ṣād, which is a collective noun, not a broken plural, because it is not one of its patterns." He said: "The counterpart of this word is qinw and qinwān, and no third is found for them."
(الْأُكُلِ): with ḍamma or sukūn on the kāf. In al-Miṣbāḥ: al-ukul, with two ḍammas, the second made quiescent for lightness: what is eaten.

* I'rab:
(المر تِلْكَ آياتُ الْكِتابِ): (المر): its i'rab and the discussion of it, and of the openings of the suras in general, have preceded. The demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (آيات الكتاب) the khabar (predicate).
(وَالَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ الْحَقُّ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction, conjoining clauses to clauses. (الذي) is the mubtadaʾ and the clause (أنزل إليك) the ṣila (relative clause); (من ربك) is a preposition and its genitive noun also attached to (أنزل); and (الحق) is the khabar of (الذي). (ولكن): the wāw is circumstantial, and (لكن) is a particle of rectification (istidrāk) and of the accusative; (أكثر الناس) is its noun and the clause (لا يؤمنون) its predicate.
(اللَّهُ الَّذِي رَفَعَ السَّماواتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَها): (الله) is the mubtadaʾ and (الذي) its khabar; it may also be a naʿt (adjective), with the khabar coming later. The clause (رفع السموات) is the ṣila. (بغير عمد): this preposition and its genitive noun is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (السموات), that is, He raised them free of pillars. The clause (ترونها) has two aspects: the first is that it is resumptive, with the pronoun referring to the nūn [Translator's note: so in the source; the pronoun «ها» refers to the heavens], or in the accusative as a ḥāl from (السموات), that is, visible to you. It may also be an adjective of (عمد), if the pronoun refers to it. The whole sentence is resumptive, brought in to begin mentioning the proofs of the upper world as a preface to mentioning the proofs of the lower world.
(ثُمَّ اسْتَوى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ يَجْرِي لِأَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى): (ثم) is a conjunction for sequence with delay; (استوى) is a past verb with a latent agent; (على العرش) is attached to (استوى); (وسخر الشمس والقمر) is conjoined to (استوى). (كل) is a mubtadaʾ — the discussion of what permits beginning with it has preceded — and the clause (يجري) is the khabar; (لأجل) is attached to (يجري), and (مسمى) is an adjective.
(يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ يُفَصِّلُ الْآياتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ بِلِقاءِ رَبِّكُمْ تُوقِنُونَ): the clause is resumptive, or the khabar of (الله) as mentioned above. (يدبر الأمر) is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (يفصل الآيات) is conjoined. (لعل) and its noun; (بلقاء ربكم) is attached to (توقنون), and the clause (توقنون) is the khabar of (لعلكم).
(وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَدَّ الْأَرْضَ وَجَعَلَ فِيها رَواسِيَ وَأَنْهاراً): (هو) is the mubtadaʾ and (الذي) its khabar; the clause (مدّ الأرض) is the ṣila; (جعل) is conjoined to (مدّ); (فيها) is attached to (جعل); (رواسي) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and (أنهارا) is conjoined to it.
(وَمِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَراتِ جَعَلَ فِيها زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ): this preposition and its genitive noun may be attached to (جعل) after it, the implied order being "and He made in it two mates, a pair, of all fruits". It may be attached to an omitted ḥāl from (اثنين), because it was originally its adjective. Or the statement may be complete at His words (من كل الثمرات), in which case it is attached to the first (جعل), the implied meaning being that He made in the earth such-and-such and of all fruits, and the second (جعل) is resumptive. (فيها) is attached to (جعل) in every case; (زوجين) is the object of (جعل) and (اثنين) an adjective of (زوجين).
(يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهارَ): the clause is resumptive, or a ḥāl from the agent of the verbs before it. The agent of (يغشي) is latent; (الليل) is the first object and (النهار) the second object. The meaning is that He clothes it in its place, so it becomes black and dark after having been white and bright. It is more fitting for the night to be the one that covers, which is why we made it the first object, though the speech allows the second.
(إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ): (إن) and its fronted predicate; (لآيات): the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis, and (آيات) is the postponed noun of (إن); (لقوم) is an adjective of (آيات), and the clause (يتفكرون) is an adjective of (قوم).
(وَفِي الْأَرْضِ قِطَعٌ مُتَجاوِراتٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; (في الأرض) is a fronted predicate and (قطع) a postponed subject; (متجاورات) is an adjective of (قطع), that is, tracts differing and distinct from one another despite being adjacent.
(وَجَنَّاتٌ مِنْ أَعْنابٍ وَزَرْعٌ وَنَخِيلٌ صِنْوانٌ وَغَيْرُ صِنْوانٍ): (جنات) is conjoined to (قطع); (من أعناب) is an adjective; (زرع) and (نخيل) are also conjoined; (صنوان) is an adjective of (نخيل); (غير) is conjoined, and (صنوان) is the muḍāf ilayhi.
(يُسْقى بِماءٍ واحِدٍ وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَها عَلى بَعْضٍ فِي الْأُكُلِ): the clause (يسقى) is an adjective of (جنات) and what follows it; (بماء) is attached to (يسقى) and (واحد) is an adjective of (ماء). (نفضل بعضها) is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (على بعض) is attached to (نفضل); (في الأكل) is a ḥāl from (بعضها), that is, We make some of them excel as something eaten, or [Translator's note: the source has «أو وفيه الأكل», apparently corrupt] … It may also be attached to (نفضل), since it is an adverb (ẓarf) for it.
(إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ): the i'rab of its counterpart has preceded just above.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «ثم استوى على العرش» there is an implicit (makniyya) or imaginative (takhyīliyya) metaphor, according to the definition of the ancients. The thing borrowed is the "settling" (istiwāʾ); that from which it is borrowed is every body that settles; and that for which it is borrowed is the Truth, Glorified is He. [This is] so that the hearer, on hearing the wording of this metaphor, imagines a king who has finished arranging his realms and building up his kingdom and everything his subjects and soldiers need — the cultivation of his lands and the management of the affairs of his servants — and then settles upon the throne of his kingdom in a settling of majesty. The hearer thus measures what is absent from his senses of the matter of divinity by what is imagined. For this reason the settling on the Throne is mentioned only after finishing the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, even though there is no throne set up there, nor any perceptible sitting, nor any settling in the sense the outward wording indicates of defining a particular posture.
2- In His words «بغير عمد ترونها» there is a lofty art mentioned earlier, namely negating a thing by affirming it [Translator's note: i.e. what is called «نفي الشيء بإيجابه»], that is, He raised the heavens free of pillars; the sense is the negation of both the pillars and the seeing together: there is no seeing and no pillars.
This verse has stirred in the mind the subject of the conquest of the moon, and how man explored space and saw the wonders of Allah's making, and witnessed the earth suspended, and the moon suspended, and likewise the planets and the other stars suspended without any support to prop them up or pillars on which they stand — confirming the words of Allah «بغير عمد ترونها».

dervis-irab:5-6.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْمَثُلاتُ): plural of mathula, with fatḥa on the mīm and ḍamma on the thāʾ. In al-Qāmūs: al-mathula is punishment, and the torment that befell past generations; they are lessons from which a lesson is drawn. Al-Zamakhsharī explained it in a fine way, saying: it is called mathula because of the likeness (mumāthala) between the punishment and what is punished. Someone else said: al-mathula is a vengeance that comes down on a person, so that he is made an example (mithāl) by which others are deterred. Ibn al-Anbārī said: al-mathula, on the pattern of samura, is the punishment that leaves something in the one punished by altering part of his form, from their saying «مثل فلان بفلان» when someone disfigures another's form by cutting off his nose, gouging out his eyes and slitting open his belly.

* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ تَعْجَبْ فَعَجَبٌ قَوْلُهُمْ): the wāw is resumptive; (إن) is conditional; (تعجب) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its agent is latent, its implied form being "you, O Muhammad". The fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa); (عجب) is a fronted predicate and (قولهم) a postponed subject; and the clause (فعجب قولهم) is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the jussive-governing condition.
(أَإِذا كُنَّا تُراباً أَإِنَّا لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ): this clause is the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and you may parse it as a badal (substitute) from it. The hamza is for the interrogation of denial. (إذا) is an adverb of future time, putting its condition in the genitive and attached to its reply, which is what His words (أإنا لفي خلق جديد) indicate, the implied form being "we will be raised" or "gathered". Abū Ḥayyān preferred that (إذا) be purely an adverb without any sense of condition; what governs it is then omitted and explained by what the second clause indicates, its implied form being "Will we be raised?" or "Will we be gathered?". (كنا) is (كان) and its noun, and (ترابا) is its predicate. (أإنا): the hamza is for the interrogation of denial; (إن) and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (في خلق) is the predicate of (إن); and (جديد) is an adjective of (خلق).
(أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ): (أولئك) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الذين) its khabar (predicate); the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause), and (بربهم) is attached to (كفروا).
(وَأُولئِكَ الْأَغْلالُ فِي أَعْناقِهِمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; (الأغلال) is a second mubtadaʾ; (في أعناقهم) is the khabar of (الأغلال); and the second mubtadaʾ with its khabar is the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ. Al-aghlāl is the plural of ghull, a collar of iron placed on the neck.
(وَأُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ): the wāw is also a conjunction; (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ and (أصحاب النار) its khabar; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ, (فيها) is attached to (خالدون), and (خالدون) is its khabar. The clause (هم فيها خالدون) is a second khabar of (أولئك), or a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ الْحَسَنَةِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (يستعجلونك) is a verb, an agent and a direct object; and (بالسيئة) is attached to (يستعجلونك), because it is an adverb (ẓarf) of the hastening. [Translator's note: so in the source; the explanation "because it is an adverb of the hastening" evidently belongs to (قبل), which is a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial) attached to (يستعجلونك); the source does not parse (قبل الحسنة) separately.]
(وَقَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمُ الْمَثُلاتُ): the wāw is circumstantial; (قد) is a particle of realization; (خلت) is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents; (من قبلهم) is attached to (خلت); and (المثلات) is the fāʿil (agent) of (خلت).
(وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِلنَّاسِ عَلى ظُلْمِهِمْ): the wāw is also circumstantial; (إن) and its noun; the shifted lām; (ذو مغفرة) is the predicate of (إن); (للناس) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (مغفرة); (على ظلمهم) is a ḥāl from (الناس), and what governs it is (مغفرة), since it governs the one to whom the ḥāl refers. The meaning is "while wronging themselves", and the meaning of (على) here is accompaniment, that is, like (مع).
(وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَشَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) and its noun; the shifted lām; and (شديد العقاب) is its predicate.

* Benefits:
In this verse there is one of the arts of the Arabs in their speech, namely inversion (al-qalb), in His words «وأولئك الأغلال في أعناقهم», because it is the necks that are in the shackles and not the reverse. Of it is the saying of Ruʾba:
ومهمه مغبرة أرجاؤه ... كأن لون أرضه سماؤه
(Many a desert whose horizons are dust-coloured, as if the colour of its ground were its sky.)
that is, as if the colour of its sky were the colour of its ground; so he reversed the simile for hyperbole and omitted the muḍāf.

dervis-irab:7-11.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْأَرْحامُ): plural of raḥim, with fatḥa on the rāʾ and kasra on the ḥāʾ, or with kasra on the rāʾ and sukūn on the ḥāʾ: the place where the fetus is deposited in the insides of the pregnant woman. It is feminine. Al-raḥim is also kinship; what is meant here is the first.
(سارِبٌ): going on his sarb, with fatḥa, that is, on his road and in his direction. One says «سرب في الأرض سروبا». In al-Miṣbāḥ: "saraba fī al-arḍ surūban, of the pattern qaʿada: he went; saraba al-māʾ surūban: the water flowed; saraba al-māl sarban: the livestock grazed by day without a herdsman, so it is sārib, and sarb, named by the maṣdar. Al-sarb is also the road, and from it one says «خلّ سربه», that is, his road. Al-sirb, with kasra, is the self; 'he is wide of sirb' means he is at ease of mind, and it is said to mean broad of breast, slow to anger. Al-sarab, with two fatḥas, is a dwelling in the ground with no outlet, that is, a den."
«معقبات»: there are two possibilities in it. One is that it is the plural of muʿaqqiba in the sense of muʿaqqib, the tāʾ being for intensiveness as in ʿallāma and nassāba, that is, an angel who follows in succession; then this was pluralised, as in ʿallāmāt and nassābāt. The second is that it is the plural of muʿaqqiba as an adjective of a group, then this adjective was pluralised, like jamal, jimāl and jimālāt. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It was also said that al-muʿaqqibāt are the guards and constables around the ruler who guard him — in his imagination — and its implied meaning is 'from the command of Allah', that is, from His decrees and calamities; or [it is said] in mockery of him."

* I'rab:
(وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ): the wāw is resumptive; (يقول الذين) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent). The speech turned from the pronoun to the relative noun in order to censure them for their disbelief in the signs of Allah. The clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause). (لولا) is a particle of urging in the sense of (هلا); (أنزل) is a past verb, passive; (عليه) is attached to (أنزل); (آية) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and (من ربه) is a naʿt (adjective) of (آية).
(إِنَّما أَنْتَ مُنْذِرٌ وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هادٍ): (إنما) is the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna]; (أنت) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (منذر) the khabar (predicate). (لكل) is a fronted predicate, (قوم) the muḍāf ilayhi, and (هاد) a postponed subject; the clause is resumptive.
(اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ما تَحْمِلُ كُلُّ أُنْثى): (الله) is the mubtadaʾ and the clause (يعلم) its khabar; the agent of (يعلم) is latent, its implied form being "He". (ما) admits three equal aspects. The first is that it is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the object of (يعلم), with the clause (تحمل كل أنثى) its ṣila and the returning pronoun omitted, that is, "carries it". The second is that it is maṣdariyya, and together with what it enters on it is the object of (يعلم); the clause after it then has no grammatical position and no returning pronoun is needed. The third is that it is interrogative: either a mubtadaʾ with the clause (تحمل) its khabar, the clause suspending [the governance of] the [verb of] knowing; or a fronted object of (تحمل).
(وَما تَغِيضُ الْأَرْحامُ وَما تَزْدادُ): conjoined to the preceding clause, and the aspects mentioned above apply to «ما». (غاض) and (زاد) are used both transitively and intransitively. The exegetes have spoken at length on the meaning of the wombs' diminishing and increasing; its gist is that what is meant is the nourishment of the child in the womb: when blood comes out the nourishment decreases and the child decreases, and when she does not menstruate the child increases and grows. It was also said that it concerns the length of pregnancy. It is better to refer to the longer works for the details.
(وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ عِنْدَهُ بِمِقْدارٍ): (كل) is the mubtadaʾ and (شيء) the muḍāf ilayhi; (عنده) is an adverb attached to an omitted adjective of (شيء) or of (كل); and (بمقدار) is the khabar. What is meant by "with Him" is knowledge of the quantity and manner of everything in detailed and clear fashion, or knowledge of the time of everything and its specific state.
(عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ الْكَبِيرُ الْمُتَعالِ): (عالم الغيب) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "He"; (الغيب) is the muḍāf ilayhi and (الشهادة) is conjoined; (الكبير) is a second khabar of the omitted mubtadaʾ and (المتعال) a third khabar. It was written without a yāʾ because it is a verse-ending; were it not for that, the better form would be to retain it.
(سَواءٌ مِنْكُمْ مَنْ أَسَرَّ الْقَوْلَ وَمَنْ جَهَرَ بِهِ): (سواء) may be a fronted predicate, with (منكم) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from its pronoun and (من), a relative noun, the postponed subject; it was originally a maṣdar in the sense of mustawin (equal), and the discussion of it has preceded in al-Baqara. It may also be a mubtadaʾ, with (منكم) an adjective and (من) the khabar. The clause (أسر القول) is the ṣila, that is, he concealed it within himself; and (من جهر به) is conjoined to (من أسر القول).
(وَمَنْ هُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍ بِاللَّيْلِ وَسارِبٌ بِالنَّهارِ): (ومن) is conjoined to the preceding (من); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (مستخف) the khabar, and the nominal clause is the ṣila; (بالليل) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (مستخف); (سارب) is conjoined to (مستخف), and (بالنهار) is attached to (سارب). The regular form of the speech would be "and whoever is sārib". The secret in it is that the relative noun was omitted while its ṣila remained, the meaning being "and whoever is hiding by night and whoever goes forth by day". Omitting a conjoined relative noun while keeping its ṣila is common, especially as the relative noun is repeated three times in the verse. Of it are His words «وما أدري ما يفعل بي ولا بكم», the original being «ولا ما يفعل بكم»; otherwise the negative particle would be an intruder out of its place, because if the second clause were taken to be included in the ṣila of the first by means of the conjunction, the prohibition [Translator's note: so in the source, «للنهي»; the sense requires "the negation"] would have no place; it accompanied, in the first, the relative noun, not the ṣila. Of it is the saying of Ḥassān:
فمن يهجو رسول الله منكم ... ويمدحه وينصره سواء
(Whoever among you satirises the Messenger of Allah, and [whoever] praises him and supports him — it is all the same.)
that is, "and whoever praises him and supports him" — it is all the same.
(لَهُ مُعَقِّباتٌ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ): (له) is a fronted predicate, and the pronoun goes back to «من», as if it were said: "whoever conceals, whoever declares, whoever hides and whoever goes forth has followers in succession". (معقبات) is a postponed subject; (من بين يديه) is an adjective of (معقبات), or attached to (معقبات) itself; (من خلفه) is conjoined to (من بين يديه); the clause (يحفظونه) is also an adjective of (معقبات); and (من أمر الله) is attached to (يحفظونه). The discussion of what is meant by al-muʿaqqibāt has preceded in the vocabulary section. The meaning of (يحفظونه من أمر الله) is "from what He has commanded, because they are able to repel the command of Allah" [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense evidently requires "because they are not able to repel the command of Allah", or the clause belongs to the mocking interpretation mentioned in the vocabulary section]. Ibn al-Anbārī said: There is another view on this, namely that (من) is in the sense of the bāʾ, that is, they guard him by the command of Allah. It was also said that (من) is in the sense of (عن), that is, they guard him from (ʿan) the command of Allah, meaning from Allah, not of their own accord, as in His words «أطعمهم من جوع», that is, ʿan jūʿ. It was also said: they guard him from the angels of punishment; and it was said: they guard him from the jinn. Ibn Jarīr preferred that al-muʿaqqibāt are the processions before rulers, in the sense that that does not ward off the decree from him.
The wording of al-Farrāʾ: "There are two views on this. One is that it involves fronting and postponement, its implied order being: 'He has followers in succession from the command of Allah who guard him from before him and behind him.' The second is that the guardians' guarding him is part of what Allah has commanded."
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُغَيِّرُ ما بِقَوْمٍ حَتَّى يُغَيِّرُوا ما بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ): (إن) and its noun, and the clause (لا يغير) is its predicate; the agent of (يغير) refers to Allah; (ما) is a relative noun, the object of (يغير), and (بقوم) is the ṣila. (حتى) is a particle of limit and genitive; (يغيروا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after (حتى); (ما) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and (بأنفسهم) the ṣila.
(وَإِذا أَرادَ اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ سُوْءاً فَلا مَرَدَّ لَهُ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إذا) is an adverb of future time, putting its condition in the genitive and in the accusative by its reply; the clause (أراد الله) is annexed to it (muḍāf ilayhā); (بقوم) is attached to (أراد). The fāʾ is connective; (لا) is the lā of generic negation, (مرد) its noun and (له) its predicate. [Translator's note: the source does not parse (سوءا), the mafʿūl bihi of (أراد).]
(وَما لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ والٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (لهم) is a fronted predicate; (من دونه) is a ḥāl; (من) is redundant (zāʾida); and (وال) is genitive in form and nominative in position, because it is a postponed subject.

* Rhetoric:
1- Antithesis (al-ṭibāq) in His words «الله يعلم ما تحمل كل أنثى وما تغيض الأرحام وما تزداد», that is, what decreases and what increases.
2- Hyperbole (al-mubālagha), or excess in description (al-ifrāṭ fī al-ṣifa), the naming differing: the first is Qudāma's and the second Ibn al-Muʿtazz's, and people follow Qudāma's naming. Qudāma defined it, saying: it is that the speaker mentions a state which, had he stopped at it, would have sufficed; but he does not stop at it until he adds to the meaning of his speech something more forceful in conveying what he intends. It has numerous kinds, which we give briefly below:
a- Hyperbole in an adjective diverted from the regular [participle] for the sense of intensiveness. It comes in six patterns: faʿlān, such as raḥmān, diverted from rāḥim for intensiveness, as preceded in the basmala; it is used to describe Allah the Exalted alone, and the Arabs did not describe anyone by it, either in the Jāhiliyya or in Islam, except Musaylima the Liar, whom they described by it, and their poet said:
سموت بالمجد يا ابن الأكرمين أبا ... فأنت غيث الورى لا زلت رحمانا
(You rose high in glory, O son of the noblest in lineage; you are the rain of mankind — may you ever remain raḥmān.)
As for al-Raḥmān [with the article], no one has been described by it except Allah.
Faʿʿāl, as in His words «وإني لغفار لمن تاب».
Faʿūl, as in ghafūr, shakūr and wadūd.
Faʿīl, as in ʿalīm, ḥakīm and samīʿ.
Mifʿal, as in midʿas, on the pattern of minbar: the spear with which one thrusts (yudʿas), as in Tāj al-ʿArūs.
Mifʿāl, as in miṭʿām and miqdām.
b- What comes in the general form in place of the particular, as when you say "All the people came to me" when only one of them came to you, intending to magnify him. Of it are His words:
«إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب»: the Glorified promised them a reward not measured out, by casting the expression in general form, so that minds waver about the amount of the reward.
c- Casting the speech in the form of a report about the greatest, most supreme [being] for hyperbole, as in His words «وجاء ربك والملك صفا صفا»: He made the coming of His signs a coming of Himself, Glorified is He.
d- Moving the condition from the possible to the impossible so that the occurrence of the conditioned thing is impossible, as in His words in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf, which has preceded: «ولا يدخلون الجنة حتى يلج الجمل في سم الخياط».
e- What runs as literal though it was figurative, as in His words:
«يكاد سنا برقه يذهب بالأبصار»: the joining of this clause with (يكاد) turns it toward the literal, so it changed from impossibility to possibility.
This is overt hyperbole in all these kinds. There is, however, an embedded (mudmaja) hyperbole, namely His words in the verse we are dealing with: «سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به ومن هو مستخف بالليل وسارب بالنهار», for the hyperbole of this verse came embedded in the correspondence (al-muqābala).
More on hyperbole and its kinds will come in scattered places in this book.

* Benefits:
The exegetes almost agree that this verse indicates that when a people lives in blessing, Allah does not change it for them unless they disobey their Lord and wrong one another. The corollary of this interpretation is that blessing lasts and increases through gratitude and obedience, and that it vanishes through ingratitude and tyranny. There was, and still is, something in the mind about this interpretation, for several reasons:
First: we see that monopolists and exploiters, the more active they are in tyranny, plunder and pillage, the more their wealth multiplies and grows.
Second: this interpretation conflicts with the words of Allah the Exalted in the thirty-third verse of Sūrat al-Zukhruf: «ولولا أن يكون الناس أمة واحدة لجعلنا لمن يكفر بالرحمن لبيوتهم سقفا من فضة ومعارج عليها يظهرون، ولبيوتهم أبوابا وسررا عليها يتكئون، وزخرفا وإن كل ذلك لما متاع الحياة الدنيا والآخرة عند ربك للمتقين». So abundance of provision does not indicate Allah's pleasure, just as straitness does not signal His anger, for He does not reward the grateful with gold and silver nor punish the disobedient by depriving them of them; rather the matter is the reverse, for it has come in the Noble Qur'an that Allah punishes the ungrateful with abundance of wealth: «فلا تعجبك أموالهم ولا أولادهم إنما يريد الله ليعذبهم بها في الحياة الدنيا وتزهق أنفسهم وهم كافرون».
Third: it conflicts with what is transmitted and widely known, that the believer is tried and tested.
Perhaps the best interpretation the verse can bear is to say: the person who first revolts against himself and reforms it is the true reformer; and the one who [revolts] against the traditions and systems he has inherited, which may have been corrupt, or against what time has corrupted, and reforms it — he is the one who may properly be meant by this verse, in which lies the spirit of courage and of revolt against corrupt customs and traditions, corrupt beliefs and principles, against poverty and ignorance, and against colonialism and feudalism; just as there lies in it the spirit of revolt against those who build palaces from the sweat of toilers and prepare cars from the tears of the afflicted.

dervis-irab:12-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(السَّحابَ): the cloud drawn along (munsaḥib) in the air. Saḥāb is a generic noun (ism jins) whose singular is saḥāba; for that reason it is described with a plural, namely al-thiqāl, the plural of thaqīla. It is understood from the words of the author of al-Qāmūs that it is a plural of saḥāba; he said: "al-saḥāba: the cloud; plural saḥāb, saḥāʾib and suḥub."
(الْمِحالِ): al-mumāḥala, which is intense scheming and plotting. From it «تمحّل لكذا» [Translator's note: the source prints «تحمل»] when one takes pains to use a stratagem for something and exerts oneself in it; and «محل بفلان» when one plots against someone and denounces him to the ruler. From it is the hadith: «and do not make it [the Qur'an] against us an accuser (māḥil) whose word is believed». Al-Aʿshā said:
فرع نبع يهشّ في غصن المجد غزير الندى شديد المحال
(A branch of nabʿ wood, lively on the bough of glory, abundant in generosity, mighty in power/cunning.)
Perhaps its origin is al-maḥl in the sense of drought. It was also said: it is fiʿāl from al-maḥl in the sense of strength, so the mīm is radical. It was also said that its origin is mafʿal from al-ḥawl or al-ḥīla, irregularly modified. In al-Qāmūs: "Al-miḥāl, like kitāb, is plotting, seeking a thing by stratagems and management; power; disputation; torment; punishment; enmity and hostility, like al-mumāḥala; strength; severity; destruction and destroying. «محل به», with the ḥāʾ taking any of the three vowels, maḥlan and miḥālan: he plotted against him by denouncing him to the ruler. «ماحله» mumāḥalatan and miḥālan: he contended in strength with him until it became clear which of them was stronger." In al-Asās: "«ماحله»: he plotted against him; he is shadīd al-miḥāl; a mutamāḥil man: excessively tall; a mutamāḥil land: far-off." [A poet] said, describing a mare:
من المسبطرّات الجياد طمرّة ... لجوج هواها السبسب المتماحل
(One of the long-striding steeds, a leaping mare, persistent, whose desire is the far-stretching desert.)
Another said, describing a camel:
بعيد من الحادي إذا ما ترقّصت ... بنات الصّوى في السبسب المتماحل
(Far ahead of the camel-driver when the cairn-markers dance [in the mirage] in the far-stretching desert.)
Al-Zajjāj said: one says «ماحلته محالا» when you contend in strength with him until it becomes clear which of you is stronger. Ibn Qutayba said: that is, severe in plotting; its origin is from al-ḥīla, the mīm being treated like the mīm of makān, whose origin is from al-kawn. Al-Azharī said: Ibn Qutayba erred [in saying] that the mīm in it is augmentative; rather it is radical. When you see a word on the pattern fiʿāl beginning with a mīm with kasra, it is radical, as in mihād, milāk and mirās.

* I'rab:
(هُوَ الَّذِي يُرِيكُمُ الْبَرْقَ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً وَيُنْشِئُ السَّحابَ الثِّقالَ): (هو) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الذي) its khabar (predicate). (يريكم البرق) is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and its two objects, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). There is disagreement about the accusative of (خوفا) and (طمعا). It was said: as maṣdars, that is, "that you may fear with fear and hope with hope". It was said: they are two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the kāf in (يريكم), that is, "you being fearful and hopeful". They may also be two mafʿūl li-ajlihi (objects of purpose); Abū al-Baqāʾ preferred this, and al-Zamakhsharī disallowed it. His exact words are: "It is not valid for them to be objects of purpose, because they are not the act of the agent of the verb whose cause is given — except on the assumption of omitting a muḍāf, that is, 'desiring fear and hope', or in the sense of 'causing fear and causing hope'. They may be in the accusative as a ḥāl from (البرق), as if it were in itself fear and hope, or in the sense of 'a source of fear and a source of hope'; or from the persons addressed, that is, 'fearful and hopeful'. The meaning of fear and hope is that the fall of thunderbolts is feared when the lightning flashes, and rain is hoped for." Abū al-Ṭayyib said:
فتى كالسحاب الجون تخشى وترتجى ... يرجّى الحيا منها وتخشى الصواعق
(A young man like the dark clouds, feared and hoped for: from them rain is hoped for, and thunderbolts are feared.)
However, al-Zamakhsharī's disallowance is far-fetched. They can be objects of purpose on the basis that the object of purpose with a verb such as this is an agent in meaning, because when He shows them, they see. The underlying form is: "And He is the One who shows you the lightning, so you see it out of fear and hope", that is, you watch it and look out for it, at one time for the sake of fear and at another for the sake of hope. (وينشئ السحاب) is conjoined; (السحاب) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (الثقال) is an adjective of (السحاب).
(وَيُسَبِّحُ الرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ وَالْمَلائِكَةُ مِنْ خِيفَتِهِ): conjoined to what precedes. (يسبح الرعد) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); (بحمده) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. There is disagreement about this bāʾ; you will see a discussion of it in the benefits section. (الملائكة) is conjoined to (الرعد), that is, and the angels glorify out of awe and reverence for Him; so it [(من خيفته)] is attached to (يسبح), and you may put it in the accusative as a ḥāl, that is, "in awe and in fear".
(وَيُرْسِلُ الصَّواعِقَ فَيُصِيبُ بِها مَنْ يَشاءُ): (ويرسل الصواعق) is conjoined to what precedes; (فيصيب) is also conjoined; (بها) is attached to (يصيب); (من) is the direct object of (يصيب); and the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila.
(وَهُمْ يُجادِلُونَ فِي اللَّهِ وَهُوَ شَدِيدُ الْمِحالِ): the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; (هم) is the mubtadaʾ and the clause (يجادلون) the khabar; (في الله) is attached to (يجادلون). The wāw is circumstantial; (هو) is the mubtadaʾ and (شديد المحال) its khabar; and the clause is circumstantial.
(لَهُ دَعْوَةُ الْحَقِّ): (له) is a fronted predicate and (دعوة الحق) a postponed subject; it is a case of annexing the qualified noun to its adjective, that is, the true call which corresponds to reality. [Translator's note: the source has «لدعوة الحق», apparently for «الدعوة الحق».]
(وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ لا يَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهُمْ بِشَيْءٍ): (الذين) is the mubtadaʾ and the clause (يدعون) the ṣila. The pronoun in (يدعون) refers to the disbelievers, and the pronoun returning to (الذين) is omitted, that is, "whom they call upon"; this is supported by the reading of those who read «تدعون» with tāʾ. It was also said that (الذين) means the disbelievers who call, and the object of (يدعون) is omitted, that is, they call upon the idols; the returning pronoun to (الذين) is then the wāw in (يدعون). The wāw in (ولا يستجيبون) on this view refers to the omitted object of (يدعون), and on the first view to (الذين). (من دونه) is a ḥāl; the clause (لا يستجيبون) is the khabar; and (لهم) is attached to (يستجيبون), as is (بشيء).
(إِلَّا كَباسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إِلَى الْماءِ لِيَبْلُغَ فاهُ وَما هُوَ بِبالِغِهِ): (إلا) is the particle of restriction; (كباسط) is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "except a response like the response [obtained by] one who stretches out his two palms". (كفيه) is the muḍāf ilayhi of (باسط); (إلى الماء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (باسط). (ليبلغ): the lām is for cause, and (يبلغ) is an imperfect in the accusative by an implied an after the lām of cause; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (باسط). (فاه) is the direct object, the sign of its accusative being the alif because it is one of the five nouns; and the agent of (يبلغ) is the pronoun of the water. The wāw is circumstantial; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative and (هو) its noun. There is disagreement about this pronoun: it was said that it is the pronoun of the water and the hāʾ in (ببالغه) refers to the mouth; it was said that it is the pronoun of the mouth and the hāʾ in (ببالغه) refers to the water; and it was said that it is a pronoun referring to (باسط) and the hāʾ in (ببالغه) refers to the water. (ببالغه): the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (بالغه) is genitive in form and accusative in position as the predicate of (ما).
(وَما دُعاءُ الْكافِرِينَ إِلَّا فِي ضَلالٍ): the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; (ما) is negative; (دعاء الكافرين) is the mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is the particle of restriction; and (في ضلال) is the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «هو الذي يريكم البرق خوفا وطمعا» there is a splendid rhetorical art, namely "soundness of divisions" (ṣiḥḥat al-aqsām). It may be defined as exhausting the meaning in all its divisions and aspects, so that the speaker leaves none of them out. In the verse mentioned, both divisions of seeing the lightning are exhausted, since there is nothing in it [Translator's note: the source has «لبس», a misprint for «ليس»] but fear of thunderbolts and hope for rain, as we indicated in the i'rab, and there is no third to these two divisions. But merely exhausting the divisions is not counted as eloquence; rather there is something beyond that, more subtle and harder to attain, namely putting first what is more deserving of mention and more fitting to be put first. In the verse, fear is put before hope, since thunderbolts may fall from the first flash, whereas rain only comes after the flashes have followed one upon another, for their succession hardly ever fails. For this reason the Arabs would count seventy flashes and then set out in search of pasture, and they would not miss the rain and the herbage. Abū al-Ṭayyib glimpsed the sky of this lofty eloquence and said:
وقد أرد المياه بغير هاد ... سوى عدي لها برق الغمام
(I may come down to the waters without a guide other than my counting, for them, the flashes of the clouds.)
He says: I need no guide to lead me to the water except that I count the flashes of the clouds and follow them, as was the custom of the Arabs in counting the flashes of clouds. Ibn al-Sikkīt said:
"When the Arabs counted a hundred flashes, they did not doubt that it was a raining cloud that had watered [the land], so they followed it confident of rain." Ibn al-Aʿrābī said in al-Nawādir: "When lightning appeared, the Arabs would count seventy flashes; when they were complete, they were confident that it was raining lightning and set off seeking the place of the rain." And ʿUmar ibn al-Aʿwar recited:
سقى الله جيرانا حمدت جوارهم ... كراما إذا عدّوا وفوق كرام
يعدون برق المزن في كل مهمه ... فما رزقهم إلا بروق غمام
(May Allah water neighbours whose neighbourliness I praised — noble when counted, and above the noble. They count the lightning of the rain-clouds in every desert, so their provision is nothing but the flashes of clouds.)
Since the feared thing from lightning may occur from the very first flash, the mention of fear came first in the verse, because one is the first of numbers; and since the hoped-for thing from the flashes occurs only after a number of flashes, the mention of hope came second, because it occurs only in the course of counting, and so that hope might abrogate fear, like ease coming after hardship, relief after distress and joy after grief, so that it is sweeter in its effect on hearts. This interpretation is attested by His words:
«وهو الذي ينزل الغيث من بعد ما قنطوا وينشر رحتمه» [Translator's note: so in the source, for «رحمته»]. So the meaning of the verse came in the manner of mercy from Allah, Glorified is He, to His creation and good tidings to His servants.

Affinity between meanings and affinity between structures
Since we have reached this point in the ordering of divisions, it is fitting that we speak of affinity (muʾākhāh) between meanings and affinity between structures, which is the secret of eloquence and the breath of the spirit in it. They faulted Abū al-Ṭayyib's saying, though it is a wonder of beauty and splendour:
لمن تطلب الدنيا إذا لم ترد بها ... سرور محب أو مساءة مجرم
(For whom do you seek this world, if you do not intend by it the joy of a lover or the hurt of a wrongdoer?)
For the correct correspondence is between the lover and the hater [Translator's note: the source has «بن», a misprint for «بين»], not between the lover and the wrongdoer, and not everyone who wrongs you hates you.
Abū al-Faraj related in al-Aghānī that Nuṣayb, al-Kumayt and Dhū al-Rumma met, and al-Kumayt recited:
أم هل ظعائن بالعلياء رافعة ... وإن تكامل فيها الدّلّ والشنب
(Or are there litters on the heights, moving off, though coquetry and freshness of teeth are complete in them?)
Nuṣayb counted one on his fingers, and al-Kumayt said to him: "What are you counting?" He said: "Your mistake, for you went far apart in your speech: what has coquetry to do with freshness of teeth? Why did you not say as Dhū al-Rumma [Translator's note: the source prints «دو الرمة»] said:
لمياء في شفتيها حوّة لعس ... وفي اللّثات وفي أنيابها شنب
(Dark-lipped, in her lips a dusky red tint, and in her gums and her teeth freshness.)"
This is a subtle point — as we said — in which masters of verse and prose often become entangled, and it is a likely place of error, for it needs refinement of nature and keenness of insight. Abū Nuwās fell into error in his description of the cockerel, an urjūza which we shall present in the benefits section because of its charm and rarity, and because the dīwāns in our hands present it erroneously. He said:
له اعتدال وانتصاب قدّ ... وجلده يشبه وشي البرد
كأنها الهداب في الفرند ... محدودب الظهر كريم الجد
(He has an even, upright stature, and his skin resembles the embroidery of a striped cloak, as if it were the fringe on silk; arched of back, noble of grandsire.)
For mention of the back belongs to bodily form, while the grandsire belongs to lineage; he ought to have mentioned with the back something close to it and akin to it as well. Many examples of this art will appear in our book.
2- In His words «والذين يدعون من دونه لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه وما هو ببالغه» there is a splendid representational simile (tashbīh tamthīlī). He likened the disbelievers' calling upon the gods so that they may respond to them, then the deafness of the gods, their inertness and their not responding — this is the composite thing likened — to one who stretches out his palms to water so that it may reach his mouth while it is far from it, then goes to great lengths in calling, and his obsession leads him to hope that the water will respond, though it is inanimate and does not perceive: this is that to which it is likened. It was also said: they were likened, in the uselessness of their calling upon their gods, to one who wants to scoop up water with his hands to drink it [Translator's note: the source prints «لبشربه»], and stretches them out with his fingers spread, so his palms catch nothing of it and he does not attain his aim and his drink.
Abū ʿUbayda said: "That is, like one who grasps at water: he holds nothing." He said: the Arabs coin the proverb of one who strives for what he does not attain as "one grasping at water". Sībawayh recited:
فأصبحت فيما كان بيني وبينها ... من الود مثل القابض الماء باليد
(So in the love that was between her and me, I became like one grasping water with the hand.)
Another said:
وإني وإياكم وشوقا إليكم ... كقابض ماء لم تطعه أنامله
(I, with you and my longing for you, am like one grasping water whose fingertips do not obey him.)
Another said:
ومن يأمن الدنيا يكن مثل قابض ... على الماء خانته فروج الأصابع
(Whoever trusts the world is like one grasping water, betrayed by the gaps between his fingers.)

* Benefits:
1- Disagreement over the bāʾ:
The grammarians and parsers disagreed about the bāʾ in His words «ويسبح الرعد بحمده». It was said: it is for accompaniment, or for association (mulābasa), or the bāʾ of ḥāl, that is, it glorifies Him praising Him: it declares Him free of what does not befit Him and affirms for Him what befits Him. The criterion for this bāʾ is that a ḥāl can replace it and what accompanies it, as you saw, or that «مع» fits well in its place. It was said: it is for seeking aid (istiʿāna), that is, it glorifies Him with that by which He praised Himself, so the praise is annexed to the agent, whereas on the first view it is annexed to the object. Strangely, the grammarian Ibn Khālawayh, in his book "Iʿrāb thalāthīn sūra min al-Qur'an al-karīm", when parsing «فسبح بحمد ربك», parsed it as redundant, and I do not know how he found that acceptable, for the places where the bāʾ is redundant are known, and this is not one of them.

«سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك»:
Ibn Hishām said in Mughnī al-Labīb: There is disagreement about «سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك»: it was said that it is a single clause — and the Mughnī does not mean the disagreement about the bāʾ but about the wāw — "on the basis that the wāw is redundant; and it was said that it is two clauses, on the basis that it is a conjunction, and what the bāʾ is attached to is omitted, that is, 'with Your praise I have glorified You'. Al-Khaṭṭābī said: the meaning is: 'and with Your help, which is a blessing that obliges me to praise You, I have glorified You, not by my own power and strength'." He means that it is one of the cases where the effect is put in place of the cause.

2- The ode of Abū Nuwās describing the cockerel:
We promised you to set down Abū Nuwās's [Translator's note: the source prints «نواسس»] urjūza describing the cockerel, and in fulfilment of the promise we set it down as we have seen it, differently from how it appears in the dīwāns:
أنعت ديكا من ديوك الهند ... أحسن من طاووس قطر المهدي
أسجع من عادي عرين الأسد ... ترى الدجاج حوله كالجند
يقعين منه خيفة للسّفد ... له سقاع كدويّ الرّعد
منقاره كالمعول المحدّ ... يقهر ما ناقره بالنقد
عيناه منه في القفا والخد ... ذو هامة وعنق كالورد
وجلدة تشبه وشي البرد ... ظاهرها زفّ شديد الوقد
كأنه الهدّاب في الفرند ... مضمّر الخلق عميم القدّ
له اعتدال وأنصاب قد ... محدودب الظهر كريم الجدّ
(I describe a cockerel of the cockerels of India, finer than the peacock of al-Mahdī's land; bolder than the one who attacks the lion's lair. You see the hens around him like an army, crouching before him in fear of his mounting. He has a crowing like the rumble of thunder; his beak is like a sharpened pickaxe, overpowering whatever pecks against it with its pecking. His eyes are set at the nape and the cheek; he has a crest and a neck like the rose, and a skin like the embroidery of a striped cloak, its outside down of fierce blaze, as if it were the fringe on silk; lean of build, full of stature; he has an even, upright stature, arched of back, noble of grandsire.) [Translator's note: the line division of the last verses is disordered in the source; it is given here in its evident order.]

dervis-irab:15-18.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الغدو): plural of ghudwa, with ḍamma on the ghayn; it is also pluralised as ghudā. [Also] al-ghadāh, with fatḥa on the ghayn, pluralised as ghadawāt, and al-ghadiyya, pluralised as ghadāyā and ghadiyyāt: early morning, or the time between dawn and sunrise.
(الْآصالِ): plural of al-aṣīl, the time between the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr) and sunset (maghrib). It is also pluralised as āṣāl, aṣāʾil, uṣul and uṣlān.
(احتمل): that is, ḥamala (he carried); so iftaʿala is in the sense of the bare form, or it is in the sense of the reflexive-passive (muṭāwiʿ), as understood from the wording of al-Asās: "I carried (ḥamaltu) the thing, and someone else loaded me with it, so I bore it (iḥtamaltuhu) and took it upon myself. And figuratively: I bore (ḥamaltu) her coquetry towards me and put up with it (iḥtamaltuhu). [A poet] said:
أدلّت فلم أحمل وقالت فلم أجب ... لعمر أبيها انني لظلوم
(She was coquettish and I did not bear it; she spoke and I did not answer — by her father's life, I am indeed unjust.)"
(زَبَداً): al-zabad is the scum (waḍar) of boiling. Al-waḍar, with two fatḥas and with the dotted ḍād, is the dirt of grease and the like. The wording of al-Khāzin: "Al-zabad is what rises on the surface of water when it increases, like bubbles, and likewise what rises on a pot when it boils. The meaning is: so the torrent that arose from that water carried a swelling foam, that is, high, raised above the water, floating on it." In al-Qāmūs: "Al-zabad is the froth that rises on the surface of water and the like." Among its meanings is impurity, and from it is the proverb «صرّح المخض عن الزبد» [Translator's note: the proverb is usually cited as «صرّح المحض عن الزبد»] — by al-zabad they mean the froth of milk; it is applied to truth that emerges after a doubtful report.
(جُفاءً): Ibn al-Anbārī [Translator's note: the source prints «الأنباي»] said: al-jufāʾ is what is scattered; one says «جفأت الريح السحاب», that is, the wind broke up the clouds and tore them apart. It was also said: al-jufāʾ is what the torrent throws out; one says «جفأت القدر بزبدها» (the pot cast out its scum), tajfaʾu, of the pattern qaṭaʿa; and «جفأ السيل بزبده» and «أجفأ», and «أجفل» with lām. There are two views about the hamza of jufāʾ: the more evident is that it is radical, since it is found in the derived forms of this root; the second is that it replaces a wāw. In al-Asās: "The foam went off as jufāʾ, that is, pushed away and thrown out, the valley having cast it to its sides. One says «جفأت القدر بزبدها». And a jufāʾ of the army passed to the night attack, that is, a group set apart from its main body. And you say 'he treated him with jufāʾ' and 'cast him off as jufāʾ' when he removed him from his company."
Abū ʿUbayda related that he heard Ruʾba reading «جفالا». Abū ʿUbayda said: one says "the pot ajfalat when it threw out its scum, and the wind ajfalat the clouds when it broke them up." Abū Ḥātim said: Ruʾba's reading is not to be read, because he used to eat mice.

* I'rab:
(وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ طَوْعاً وَكَرْهاً): the wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, brought to show the submission of all creatures and all beings to the creating, governing power, and their being disposed according to His will in motion and stillness, extension and disappearance, or [the shadows'] lengthening and contracting. (لله) is attached to (يسجد); (من) is the fāʿil (agent) of (يسجد); (في السموات والأرض) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (من); and (طوعا وكرها) are in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, willing and unwilling, or as maṣdars, that is, a submission of willingness and a submission of unwillingness.
(وَظِلالُهُمْ بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْآصالِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ظلالهم) is conjoined to (من); and (بالغدو والآصال) is attached to (يسجد).
(قُلْ: مَنْ رَبُّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلِ اللَّهُ): (قل) is an imperative verb whose agent is "you", and the clause after it is the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (من) is an interrogative noun, the mubtadaʾ (subject), and (رب السموات والأرض) the khabar (predicate). (قل) is an imperative verb, and (الله) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "He is Allah", or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, that is, «لله رب السموات والأرض» [Translator's note: so in the source; the intended form is evidently «الله رب السموات والأرض»].
(قُلْ أَفَاتَّخَذْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِياءَ لا يَمْلِكُونَ لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ نَفْعاً وَلا ضَرًّا): the hamza is for the interrogation of denial and mockery, and the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, as if there were an implied element between the hamza and the fāʾ, namely: "Say: have you acknowledged the said answer, and then taken…?" — this has been established many times. (اتخذتم) is a verb and its agent; (من دونه) is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of (أولياء); (أولياء) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (لا يملكون) is a naʿt (adjective); (لأنفسهم) is a ḥāl, or [attached] to (النفع) and (الضر) on the basis that they are two maṣdars; (نفعا) is the direct object, and (ولا ضرا) is conjoined to it.
(قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمى وَالْبَصِيرُ أَمْ هَلْ تَسْتَوِي الظُّلُماتُ وَالنُّورُ): (هل) is an interrogative particle in the sense of negation, that is, they are not equal. (يستوي الأعمى) is an imperfect verb and its agent; (أم) is a conjunction; and (هل تستوي الظلمات والنور) is conjoined to the preceding clause. You may make (أم) the disconnected one (munqaṭiʿa), in the sense of (بل).
(أَمْ جَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكاءَ خَلَقُوا كَخَلْقِهِ فَتَشابَهَ الْخَلْقُ عَلَيْهِمْ): (أم) is the disconnected one; (جعلوا) is a verb and its agent; (لله) is a ḥāl, because it was an adjective of (شركاء), and (شركاء) is the direct object; or (لله) is the second object of (جعلوا). The clause (خلقوا) is an adjective; the kāf with what it enters on is an adjective of an omitted object, that is, they created a creation like His creation. The fāʾ is a conjunction; (تشابه الخلق) is a past verb and its agent; and (عليهم) is attached to (تشابه).
(قُلِ اللَّهُ خالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ الْواحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ): (الله) is the mubtadaʾ and (خالق كل شيء) the khabar; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, (الواحد) the khabar, and (القهار) a second khabar.
(أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَسالَتْ أَوْدِيَةٌ بِقَدَرِها): the clause is resumptive, brought to coin a parable confirming what preceded. (أنزل) is a past verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "He", that is, Allah the Exalted; (من السماء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أنزل); (ماء) is the direct object. The fāʾ is a conjunction; (سالت أودية) is a verb and its agent; and (بقدرها) is attached to (سالت), or to an omitted adjective of (أودية), that is, according to the measure that fills them. Further discussion of it will come in the section on rhetoric.
(فَاحْتَمَلَ السَّيْلُ زَبَداً رابِياً وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ عَلَيْهِ فِي النَّارِ ابْتِغاءَ حِلْيَةٍ أَوْ مَتاعٍ زَبَدٌ مِثْلُهُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (احتمل السيل) is a past verb and its agent; (زبدا) is the object of (احتمل), because it is in the sense of (حمل); and (رابيا) is an adjective of (زبدا), that is, floating on its surface and high above it. (ومما): the wāw is a conjunction, conjoining another parable to the first parable; (مما) is a fronted predicate; the clause (يوقدون) is the ṣila; (عليه) is attached to (يوقدون); (في النار) is a ḥāl; and (ابتغاء حلية) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) according to the soundest view. It was also said to be a maṣdar in the sense of a ḥāl, that is, seeking ornament, and there is nothing to prevent that. (أو) is a conjunction and (متاع) is conjoined to (حلية). (زبد) is the postponed subject, and (مثله) is an adjective, that is, like the foam of the torrent, which is the dross that the smith's bellows expels.
(كَذلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْحَقَّ وَالْباطِلَ): (كذلك) is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, like that mentioned of the four things — two parables for the truth and two parables for falsehood: the first two are the water and the metal (al-jawhar), and the other two the foam and the dross. (يضرب الله الحق) is an imperfect verb [with its agent] and a direct object, and (الباطل) is conjoined to (الحق).
(فَأَمَّا الزَّبَدُ فَيَذْهَبُ جُفاءً): the fāʾ is a conjunction for branching out (tafrīʿ); (أما) is a particle of condition and detailing; (الزبد) is the mubtadaʾ; the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa); the clause (يذهب) is the khabar; and (جفاء) is a ḥāl.
(وَأَمَّا ما يَنْفَعُ النَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِي الْأَرْضِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (أما) is a particle of condition and detailing; (ما) is a relative noun, the mubtadaʾ; the clause (ينفع الناس) is the ṣila; the fāʾ is connective; and the clause (يمكث في الأرض) is the khabar.
(كَذلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْأَمْثالَ): its i'rab has preceded.
(لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَجابُوا لِرَبِّهِمُ الْحُسْنى): the views of the parsers differ on the i'rab of this verse. We consider that there are two preferable aspects, which we give. The first: (للذين) is a fronted predicate; the clause (استجابوا) is the ṣila; (لربهم) is attached to (استجابوا); and (الحسنى) is a postponed subject. The second: (للذين) is attached to (يضرب) in the preceding verse, and (الحسنى) is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, the goodly response.
(وَالَّذِينَ لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَهُ لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ ما فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً وَمِثْلَهُ مَعَهُ لَافْتَدَوْا بِهِ): the two foregoing parsings apply to this verse. You may make (الذين) a mubtadaʾ, so the speech is resumptive and its khabar is (لو) with what is in its scope; or you may conjoin it by coordination to the preceding (الذين). The clause (لم يستجيبوا) is the ṣila, and (له) is attached to (يستجيبوا). (لو) is conditional; (أن) with what is in its scope is the agent of an omitted verb, as has preceded. (لهم) is the predicate of (أن) and (ما) its noun; (في الأرض) is the ṣila; (جميعا) is a ḥāl; (مثله) is conjoined; and (معه) is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is, being with it. (لافتدوا): the lām falls in the reply of (لو); (افتدوا) is a past verb and the wāw its agent; and (به) is attached to (افتدوا).
(أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ سُوءُ الْحِسابِ وَمَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمِهادُ): (أولئك) is the mubtadaʾ; (لهم) is a fronted predicate and (سوء الحساب) a postponed subject, and the nominal clause is the khabar of (أولئك). (مأواهم) is a mubtadaʾ and (جهنم) the khabar of (مأواهم). (بئس) is a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; (المهاد) is the agent; and the specific object of blame is omitted, that is, "their bed", or "it".

* Rhetoric:
1- Prostration is borrowed for submission and humility — which are characteristic of rational beings — for beings rational and non-rational; [with] willingness that arises from choice, which is what issues from the human being, and unwillingness that arises without choice, which is what issues from inanimate things. The meaning of the shadows' submission is their compliance with what is wanted of them, such as their lengthening and shortening, their extending and contracting.
Abū Ḥayyān has a fine statement which we set down below to dispel misconceptions. He said:
"That the shadows are meant to be the persons [themselves], as some said, is weak; and weaker still is the saying of Ibn al-Anbārī that the Exalted gave the shadows minds with which they prostrate and humble themselves, as He gave the mountains understanding so that they addressed and were addressed. For a mountain can only have a mind on condition of supposing life, whereas the shadow is an accident in which the subsistence of life is inconceivable."
2- Mockery (al-tahakkum). The difference between it and jest by which seriousness is meant is that mockery is serious outwardly and jest inwardly, because it comes by way of derision and ridicule — this according to what is customary among us — whereas jest by which seriousness is meant is jest outwardly and serious inwardly. In His words «خلقوا كخلقه», in the context of denial, there is mockery of them, because none other than Allah creates any creation at all, whether by way of resemblance and equality or by way of inferiority and deficiency. It would have been enough, in denying them, [to say] that the partners they adopted do not create at all; but His words «كخلقه» came as mockery that adds emphasis to the denial. We have already spoken about mockery and cited verses by Ibn al-Rūmī and others on it, and we think it useful to speak a little about its opposite, namely jest by which seriousness is meant: it is when the speaker intends to praise or blame something, and casts that intention in the form of amusing jest and delightful ribaldry. The best example of it is the saying of Abū Naṣr ibn Abī al-Fatḥ Kushājim:
صديق لنا من أبدع الناس في البخل ... وأفضلهم فيه وليس بذي فضل
دعاني كما يدعو الصديق صديقه ... فجئت كما يأتي إلى مثله مثلي
فلما جلسنا للطعام رأيته ... يرى أنه من بعض أعضائه كلّيّ
ويغتاظ أحيانا ويشتم عبده ... وأعلم أن الشتم والغيظ من أجلي
فأقبلت أستل الغذاء مخافة ... وألحاظ عينيه رقيب على فعلي
أمدّ يدي سرا لأسرق لقمة ... فيلحظني شزرا فأعبث بالبقل
إلى أن جنت كفي لحتفي جناية ... وذلك أن الجوع أعدمني عقلي
فجرت يدي للحين رجل دجاجة ... فجرت كما جرت يدي رجلها رجلي
وقدم من بعد الطعام حلاوة ... فلم أستطع منها أمر ولا أحلي
وقمت لو اني كنت بيّتّ نية ... ربحت ثواب الصوم من عدم الأكل
(A friend of ours, among the most original of people in stinginess and the most excellent in it, though he has no excellence: he invited me as a friend invites his friend, and I came as one like me comes to one like him. When we sat down to the food I saw him regarding my kidneys as some of his own limbs. At times he grew angry and cursed his slave, and I knew the cursing and anger were on my account. So I began to slip the food away in fear, with the glances of his eyes a watchman over my doing. I stretch out my hand secretly to steal a morsel, and he eyes me askance, so I toy with the greens — until my hand committed a crime to my undoing, for hunger had robbed me of my reason: my hand at once dragged off a chicken's leg, and as my hand dragged its leg, he dragged me by my leg. After the food a sweet was brought, and I could neither swallow the bitter nor the sweet of it [Translator's note: the phrase «فلم أستطع منها أمرّ ولا أحلي» is idiomatic: "I could do nothing at all with it"]. I rose: had I made the intention overnight, I would have earned the reward of fasting from not eating.) [Translator's note: the line divisions of the second half of this poem are disordered in the source; they are given here in their evident order.]
3- The parable (al-mathal): the discussion of the current proverb has preceded. We say here that the Noble Book of Allah overflows with parables. In His words «أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا ومما يوقدون عليه في النار ابتغاء حلية أو متاع زبد مثله كذلك يضرب الله الحق والباطل فأما الزبد فيذهب جفاء وأما ما ينفع فيمكث في الأرض» [Translator's note: the source omits «الناس» after «ينفع» in this quotation] there are two parables which Allah coined for the truth and its people and for falsehood and its party. He represented the truth and its people by the water He sends down from the sky, by which people's valleys flow, so that they become fertile [Translator's note: the source prints «فتخصوصب»] and green, put forth plants and flourish, and they benefit from it with kinds of benefits; and by the metals from which they fashion ornaments and implements that lend them strength, awe, beauty and great might — and all that remains in the earth, its freshness not wearing out and its bloom not withering. And He likened falsehood, in the speed of its fading, the imminence of its disappearance and its being stripped of benefits, to the floating foam of the torrent, which the eye scorns and the sight shuns because of its uselessness, and to the dross that floats on top of the metal when it is melted. Under this splendid parable lie folded several kinds of rhetoric, which we give briefly:
a- The indefiniteness of «أودية» (valleys), because rain comes only by way of alternation between regions.
b- Precaution (al-iḥtirās) in His words «بقدرها», that is, in the measure that Allah knew to be beneficial to those rained upon and not harmful; otherwise, if it had overflowed and turned into a flood, it would have swept away the green and the dry and destroyed the tillage and the offspring.
c- The definiteness of «السيل» (the torrent), because it was understood from the verb before it, namely His words «فسالت»; had it been mentioned [there] it would have been indefinite, so when it was repeated it was repeated definite, as in "I saw a man, and I honoured the man". Thus the rule regularly applies to the indefinite noun when repeated.
d- Congruity (murāʿāt al-naẓīr) in the words water, torrent, foam and swelling, and in the words fire, metal, metallic ores, kindling, ornament and goods.
e- Embellished involution and evolution (al-laff wa-l-nashr al-muwashshā) in His words «فأما الزبد فيذهب جفاء» to the end of the verse.
Know that the point of likeness between the two foams — the foam carried by the torrent and the foam that rises on malleable bodies — is that when the soil of the earth mixed with the water and the water carried it along, it became a swelling foam on top of it. Likewise what they kindle fire upon until it melts, of malleable bodies: their origin is from the ores that grow in the earth, and soil mixes with them, so when they are melted, that soil which mixed with them becomes dross risen above them.

dervis-irab:19-24.t:
* I'rab:
(أَفَمَنْ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ الْحَقُّ كَمَنْ هُوَ أَعْمى): (أفمن): the discussion of this construction has preceded many times, and we repeat it for benefit. The hamza is for the interrogation of denial, and the fāʾ is moved back from a forward position, or it conjoins to something omitted which is what the hamza enters on, the implied form being: "Are the believer and the disbeliever equal? Is then the one who knows…". (من) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause (يعلم) the ṣila (relative clause). You have two aspects in (أنما): you may make it the restraining [mā] and the restrained [anna], so (أنزل) is a past verb, passive; (إليك) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (من ربك) is attached to (أنزل); and (الحق) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). Or you may separate (ما), parsing (أن) as a particle resembling the verb, (ما) as its noun and (الحق) as its predicate. On both aspects, (أن) and what is in its scope stand in place of the two objects of (يعلم). The kāf is a noun in the sense of (مثل), the khabar (predicate) of (من); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (أعمى) the khabar; and the nominal clause is the ṣila of (من).
(إِنَّما يَتَذَكَّرُ أُولُوا الْأَلْبابِ): (إنما) is the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna]; (يتذكر) is an imperfect verb and (أولو) its fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the wāw, because it is attached to the sound masculine plural; and (الألباب) is the muḍāf ilayhi.
(الَّذِينَ يُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ وَلا يَنْقُضُونَ الْمِيثاقَ): (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar will come later, namely His words (أولئك لهم عقبى الدار). You may parse it as a badal (substitute) from (أولي الألباب), to avoid the long separation between the subject and the predicate. The clause (يوفون) is the ṣila; (بعهد الله) is attached to (يوفون); and (ولا ينقضون الميثاق) is conjoined to the preceding clause. Seven further attributes of theirs will come, so their attributes become eight.
(وَالَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ ما أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَنْ يُوصَلَ): (الذين) is conjoined to (الذين); the clause (يصلون) is the ṣila; (ما) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (أمر الله) is the ṣila; the object of (أمر) is omitted, the implied form being "what He commanded them"; (به) is attached to (أمر); and (أن) with what is in its scope is a badal from the genitive pronoun, namely the hāʾ, that is, "its being joined".
(وَيَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ وَيَخافُونَ سُوءَ الْحِسابِ): (يخشون) is conjoined to (يصلون); (يخشون) is an imperfect verb and its agent, and (ربهم) the direct object; (يخافون) is conjoined to (يخشون), and (سوء الحساب) is the direct object.
(وَالَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا ابْتِغاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِمْ): (الذين) is conjoined to the preceding (الذين); (صبروا) is the ṣila; and (ابتغاء وجه ربهم) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). Someone said: "«والذين صبروا»: it was said to be a resumptive statement, and it was said to be conjoined to what precedes it; it is expressed in the past tense to draw attention to the fact that it must be realised."
(وَأَقامُوا الصَّلاةَ وَأَنْفَقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ سِرًّا وَعَلانِيَةً): (وأقاموا الصلاة) is conjoined; it is a verb, an agent and a direct object. (أنفقوا) is conjoined to (أقاموا); (مما) is attached to (أنفقوا); the clause (رزقناهم) is the ṣila, and it is a verb, an agent and a direct object. (سرا وعلانية) are accusative by removal of the preposition, or they are two maṣdars in the place of a ḥāl — Abū al-Baqāʾ preferred this — that is, in secret and in public. They may also be in the accusative as a ḥāl, that is, acting secretly and acting openly.
(وَيَدْرَؤُنَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ السَّيِّئَةَ): conjoined to what precedes, and with it their eight attributes are complete. (بالحسنة) is attached to (يدرءون), and (السيئة) is the direct object of (يدرءون).
(أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ): (أولئك) is the mubtadaʾ; (لهم) is a fronted predicate and (عقبى الدار) a postponed subject; the clause (لهم عقبى الدار) is the khabar of (أولئك); and the whole clause is the khabar of the first (الذين).
(جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَها وَمَنْ صَلَحَ مِنْ آبائِهِمْ وَأَزْواجِهِمْ وَذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ): (جنات عدن) is a badal from (عقبى الدار), or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "they are gardens", or a mubtadaʾ with the clause (يدخلونها) as its khabar. On the first two, the clause is circumstantial.
(ومن) is conjoined to the wāw in (يدخلونها), and there is no need to supply a pronoun, as some parsers did, since there is separation by the accusative pronoun. You may parse it as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), the wāw being the wāw of accompaniment. The clause (صلح) is the ṣila; (من آبائهم) is a ḥāl; and what follows it is conjoined to it.
(وَالْمَلائِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ كُلِّ بابٍ): the wāw is circumstantial; (الملائكة) is the mubtadaʾ and the clause (يدخلون) the khabar; (عليهم) is attached to (يدخلون), and (من كل باب) is also attached to (يدخلون).
(سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ بِما صَبَرْتُمْ فَنِعْمَ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ): (سلام) is the mubtadaʾ and (عليكم) the khabar; beginning [with an indefinite] is permitted because of the sense of supplication in it. The clause is the content of an omitted saying, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, that is, "saying". (بما صبرتم): the bāʾ is a preposition and (ما) is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar in the genitive by the bāʾ. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something omitted, the implied form being "this is because you were patient", that is, this is on account of your patience; so they are the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. Or [it is] attached to (سلام), that is, we greet you and honour you for your patience. It is reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he used to come to the graves of the martyrs at the start of every year and say: «Peace be upon you for your patience; how excellent is the final home!». The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; (نعم) is a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb for expressing praise; (عقبى الدار) is the agent of (نعم); and the specific object of praise is omitted, that is, "it".

* Rhetoric:
In His words «صبروا ابتغاء وجه ربهم» there is the art of precaution (al-iḥtirās), which has preceded. By His words «ابتغاء وجه ربهم» it is ruled out that their patience arose from love of rank and fame, or so that it might be said "How patient he is, how enduring of calamities, how steadfast in upheavals", so that enemies might not gloat over him, as in the saying of Abū Dhuʾayb:
وتجلدي للشامتين أريهم ... أني لريب الدهر لا أتزعزع
(And my show of fortitude to the gloaters: I show them that I am not shaken by the vicissitudes of fate.)
Nor [does it arise] from their belief that the matter is decreed and there is no escape from it, that there is no use in panic, no bringing back what is past and no warding off Allah's decree, as in [the poet's] saying:
ما إن جزعت ولا هلع.... ت ولا يرد بكاي زندا
(I did not grieve, nor did I panic, and my weeping does not bring back Zand.) [Translator's note: the verse is split mid-word «هلعت» across the hemistichs in the source.]

dervis-irab:25-29.t:
* Vocabulary:
(طُوبى): a maṣdar from al-ṭīb (goodness), like bushrā, rujʿā and zulfā, for the maṣdar may come on the pattern fuʿlā. Its root has yāʾ, so it is ṭuybā; the yāʾ was changed to wāw because it occurs quiescent after a ḍamma, as it was changed in mūqin and mūsir from al-yaqīn and al-yusr. The meaning of «طوبى لك» is "you have attained good [Translator's note: the source has «خير», evidently for «خيرا»] that is goodly". Its position is accusative or nominative, as when you say «طيبا لك» and «طيب لك», «سلاما لك» and «سلام لك». In al-Qāmūs: "Al-ṭūbā is the feminine of al-aṭyab; [it means] felicity, happiness, good and the best; and [it is] the plural of ṭayyiba, which is one of the rare plurals."

* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ يَنْقُضُونَ عَهْدَ اللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مِيثاقِهِ): (الذين) is the mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (ينقضون) is the ṣila (relative clause), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (عهد الله) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (من بعد ميثاقه) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَيَقْطَعُونَ ما أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَنْ يُوصَلَ): the i'rab of its counterpart has preceded.
(وَيُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ): conjoined to the preceding clauses.
(أُولئِكَ لَهُمُ اللَّعْنَةُ وَلَهُمْ سُوءُ الدَّارِ): (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate) is (لهم اللعنة) — the i'rab of its counterpart has preceded. The clause (أولئك لهم اللعنة) is the khabar of (الذين), and (لهم سوء الدار) is conjoined to (لهم اللعنة).
(اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ): (الله) is the mubtadaʾ and the clause (يبسط الرزق) the khabar; (لمن) is attached to (يبسط); the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila; and (يقدر) is conjoined to (يشاء) [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense is that (يقدر) is conjoined to (يبسط)].
(وَفَرِحُوا بِالْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause (فرحوا) is resumptive, brought to show the ugliness of their deeds despite the provision and ample blessings He poured on them. (بالحياة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (فرحوا), and (الدنيا) is an adjective of (الحياة).
(وَمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا مَتاعٌ): the wāw is circumstantial; (ما) is negative; (الحياة) is the mubtadaʾ and (الدنيا) an adjective; (في الآخرة) is a ḥāl, with a muḍāf omitted, that is, "beside the Hereafter". This «في» is for comparison (al-muqāyasa): it is the one that comes between a preceding inferior thing and a following superior thing. The implied form is "and the life of this world, being beside the Hereafter, is…". It is not permissible for «في» to be locative, because the life of this world is not in the Hereafter. (إلا) is the particle of restriction and (متاع) the khabar.
(وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ): the wāw is a conjunction, so that the link between their saying and the misguidance they were in runs in sequence.
(يقول الذين) is an imperfect verb and its agent; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila; (لولا) is a particle of urging equivalent to (هلا); (أنزل) is a past verb, passive; (عليه) is attached to (أنزل), and the pronoun refers to the Prophet Muhammad, upon him be peace; (آية) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and (من ربه) is a naʿt (adjective).
(قُلْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَهْدِي إِلَيْهِ مَنْ أَنابَ): (إن) and its noun, and the clause (يضل) is its predicate; (من) is the direct object and the clause (يشاء) the ṣila; (يهدي) is conjoined to (يضل); (إليه) is attached to (يهدي); (من) is the direct object and the clause (أناب) the ṣila.
(الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمْ بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ أَلا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ): (الذين) is a badal (substitute), and the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; or (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (الذين آمنوا) [in the next verse]; the first is preferable. In (تطمئن) the speech turned from the past to the imperfect to convey renewal; further discussion of it will come in the section on rhetoric. (قلوبهم) is the agent of (تطمئن); (بذكر الله) is attached to (تطمئن); and (القلوب) is the agent. [Translator's note: the source does not parse (ألا), the particle of opening and alerting.]
(الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ طُوبى لَهُمْ وَحُسْنُ مَآبٍ): (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ, or the khabar of the first (الذين). The clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila, and (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to the ṣila. (طوبى) is a mubtadaʾ and (لهم) the khabar; beginning with it is permitted because of the sense of supplication in it. It was also said that (طوبى) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the lām in (لهم) being for clarification, as in «سقيا لك» and «رعيا لك»; or it is the object of an omitted verb, that is, "you have attained goodly good". (وحسن مآب) was read in the accusative and the nominative. You may parse it [Translator's note: the antecedent of "it" appears to be (طوبى)] as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), as we stated before, on the reading of those who put (حسن) in the accusative, because the case vowel appears on it; but the first is preferable, because the majority read the nominative. Abū al-Baqāʾ made an error regarding it, since he permitted parsing it as an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), and I do not know what his justification is. (حسن) is conjoined to (طوبى), and (مآب) is the muḍāf ilayhi.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «الذين آمنوا وتطمئن قلوبهم» there is a lofty rhetorical art which has been mentioned before; we now repeat what relates to this verse. He turned away from conjoining a past verb to a past verb and did not say «واطمأنت قلوبهم», for one of the secrets that is subtle except to those who know the secrets of this noble language. Namely, among the properties of the imperfect verb is that no specific time, present or future — the two times the imperfect can bear — may be considered in it, so that it indicates nothing but mere continuity. Of this is this verse: that is, the believers' hearts find rest constantly, however much trials follow one another, calamities succeed each other and surprises occur — as if they had prepared for every trial a patience and for every calamity a fresh rest. Reflect on this observation, for it is the pillar of the beauty and its secret.

dervis-irab:30-31.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَيْأَسِ): al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning of «أفلم ييأس» is 'did they not know?'. It was said: it is the dialect of a tribe of al-Nakhaʿ. It was also said: despair (al-yaʾs) was used in the sense of knowledge only because one who despairs of a thing knows that it will not be, just as hope (al-rajāʾ) was used in the sense of fear, and forgetting in the sense of leaving." Suḥaym ibn Wathīl al-Riyāḥī said:
أقول لهم بالشعب إذ ييسرونني ... ألم تيئسوا أني ابن فارس زهدم
(I say to them in the mountain pass, as they are dividing me up [as spoil]: do you not know that I am the son of the rider of Zahdam?)
In al-Mukhtār: "Al-yaʾs is despondency; yaʾisa min al-shayʾ, of the pattern fahima. There is another dialect form: yaʾisa yayʾisu, with kasra in both, which is irregular. Yaʾisa is also in the sense of ʿalima (he knew) in the dialect of al-Nakhaʿ, and from it are His words: «أفلم ييئس الذين آمنوا»."
